messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for dedicated-pool-12 (region-us-west). Metric spike at ~2198765420. Streaming requests showing stalls and long tail. Paging ops-oncall. :rotating_light:
Priya Patel: I'm on it — taking incident commander. first pass: any obvious throttles or scaling events?
Ethan Kim: seeing sustained queue_depth > 120 for pool-12, autoscaler triggered scale-up at 2198765415 but new nodes stayed in PENDING for 20-30s. Handshake logs show many warmup connections timing out.
Maya Ruiz: corroborating — streaming p95 ~800ms -> p99 ~6.2s, lots of gRPC stream stall traces. KV cache miss rate spiked.
Priya Patel: is this a coldstart/warmup problem or capacity exhaustion? need quick mitigation for customer impact.
Ethan Kim: root cause looks like twofold: (1) a burst of traffic pinned requests to a small subset of pinned instances (queue pinning) and (2) autoscaler handshake had a delay because warmup health checks failed during image pull spikes. In short: autoscale delayed and the running replicas were saturated.
Lena (Customer Ops): Customer-hosted app team reported many truncated streaming responses and timeouts around 10:15 PDT. They're seeing p99 > 5s and are asking if we can route to fallback model.
Marco Chen: can we flip traffic to a cheaper smaller variant in the region while we recover? fallback routing exists but needs manual enable for pool-12.
Priya Patel: mitigation plan now: 1) manually add 4 reserved replicas to pool-12, 2) enable automatic fallback to model-psi-small for streaming routes, 3) temporarily enable request-dropping after queue depth 200 to preserve availability. Who can run the manual scale?
Ethan Kim: I can scale manually. Running command now:```sh
# scale dedicated pool
redwoodctl pools scale --pool pool-12 --replicas 4 --reason "incident-2198765432 emergency scale"
```
Ethan Kim: scale command accepted; new replicas provisioning. Watching for podReady.
Maya Ruiz: enabling fallback routing (canary route) now. Marco can confirm traffic shift.
Marco Chen: enabled fallback routing for streaming.* -> model-psi-small for pool-12. Rolling traffic over 10s. Notifying Customer Ops.
Lena (Customer Ops): shared note to customers: "We detected a latency incident affecting streaming in US-WEST. We have added temporary capacity and routed traffic to a smaller fallback model while we stabilize. Expect degraded throughput but lower latency. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."
ops-oncall: Observed new replicas Ready at +32s from scale command. p95 dropped to ~220ms within one minute, p99 trending down now ~900ms.
Priya Patel: Good. Are we still seeing streaming stalls/tail traces? Maya?
Maya Ruiz: stalls reduced but not gone; still seeing tail events caused by in-flight requests pinned to instances that were performing heavy prefix cache loads. Need to investigate KV cache priming codepath.
Ethan Kim: the autoscaler handshake logs show transient failures of the warmup probe to complete during image pulls when registry rates spiked; warmup timeout is currently 15s. Propose increasing warmup handshake timeout to 30s and enabling parallel warmup connections so a single slow instance doesn't block the autoscale completion.
Priya Patel: set immediate actions and longer term items. Immediate (owner):
- Ethan: confirm all scaled replicas healthy and keep fallback routing until p99 < 400ms for 10m.
- Maya: collect 5 sample tail traces and attach to incident thread.
- Marco + Lena: customer comms follow-up with expected ETA.
Longer term proposals (for postmortem):
- Increase warmup handshake timeout to 30s and add exponential backoff on the probe.
- Add autoscaler metric for handshake success rate and surface an alert when handshake success < 90% during scale events.
- Revisit prefix cache priming to avoid heavy priming on a few nodes (spread priming).
- Consider pre-warming small standby capacity for major pools to avoid the first-burst coldstart.
Ethan Kim: confirmed replicas healthy. Keeping fallback routing on; will flip off only when p99 < 400ms for 10m.
Maya Ruiz: attached sample traces (pasting key snippet):```json
{
  "trace_id": "abc123",
  "span": "streaming_send",
  "dur_ms": 4879,
  "notes": "KV cache priming on large prefix, repeated disk reads"
}
```
Priya Patel: escalation/hand-off: I'm handing this off to eng-runtime for full postmortem. ops-oncall stays monitoring for next 2 hours. Maya & Ethan you are action owners. I'll update the incident status to 'mitigated' when p99 stabilizes under threshold.
Marco Chen: noted — logging a follow-up ticket in backlog for the priming change and autoscaler metrics. Linking to postmortem.
Lena (Customer Ops): customers updated. one large customer asked about SLA credits; will route to sales/legal after postmortem.
Priya Patel: summary for incident doc: "Capacity saturation + autoscale handshake delays caused temporary p99 SLO breach for pool-12. Immediate mitigations: manual scale and fallback routing reduced p99 from ~6s -> ~0.9s, customers routed to fallback model. Postmortem to cover warmup timeout, registry throttling impact, and prefix cache priming."
ops-oncall: continuing to monitor. marking this thread for postmortem labeling and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
